# Chronic wounds

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Infectious diseases > Wound, soft tissue, bone, and joint infections > Chronic wounds*

[Original Article Link](/library/zw0rlR)

---

## Summary

Chronic wounds are wounds that do not begin to heal within 4 weeks despite appropriate care. They are caused by cessation or disruption of one of the <u>phases of wound healing</u>, typically the inflammation phase. Chronic wounds most commonly occur in older adults and individuals with <u>diabetes</u>, <u>peripheral arterial disease</u>, <u>chronic venous insufficiency</u>, prolonged <u>immobilization</u>, or <u>malnutrition</u>. Diagnosis involves assessing for underlying <u>risk factors</u> and complications such as infection, as well as <u>biopsy</u> in selected cases. Management is multifactorial and includes treatment of the underlying cause (e.g., <u>diabetes</u>) and meticulous local wound care with regular <u>debridement</u>, maintenance of appropriate moisture balance, and <u>infection control</u>.




This article provides an overview of chronic wounds; see “<u>Chronic venous disease</u>,” “<u>Peripheral arterial disease</u>,” “<u>Diabetic foot ulcers</u>,” and “<u>Decubitus ulcers</u>” for more detailed information on specific wound types.

---

## Pathophysiology

* Chronic wounds develop due to cessation or disruption of one of the <u>phases of wound healing</u> (most commonly the resorptive, or inflammation, phase).

* Most commonly occurs in patients with multiple <u>risk factors for delayed wound healing</u>

* The proliferative <u>wound healing phase</u> is delayed in individuals with <u>copper</u> and <u>vitamin C deficiency</u>.

* <u>Zinc deficiency</u> can delay <u>wound healing</u> because the <u>collagenases</u> responsible for <u>collagen</u> remodeling require <u>zinc</u> for proper function.





> [!NOTE]
> All chronic wounds begin as <u>acute wounds</u>.

---

## Risk factors

There are multiple <u>risk factors for delayed wound healing</u>, including: [[1]](/library/mAdV4s0)[[3]](/library/MAdM4s0)




* Systemic factors

* Chronic systemic diseases (e.g., <u>diabetes mellitus</u>, <u>chronic liver disease</u>, <u>chronic kidney disease</u>, <u>connective tissue disease</u>)

* <u>Malnutrition</u> (e.g., deficiency of <u>zinc</u>, <u>copper</u>, <u>vitamin C</u>; <u>hypoproteinemia</u>) [[1]](/library/mAdV4s0)[[4]](/library/bZVHZG0)

* Medications (e.g., <u>steroids</u>, cytotoxics, and other <u>immunosuppressants</u> including <u>bevacizumab</u>) [[5]](/library/CZVqdG0)

* High <u>cortisol</u> levels [[6]](/library/dZVo0G0)

* <u>Hypothermia</u> [[7]](/library/LAdw4s0)

* <u>Phagocyte</u> <u>immunodeficiencies</u> (e.g., <u>leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1</u>) [[8]](/library/VZVG0G0)

* Regional factors

* Infection

* Insufficient arterial supply (e.g., <u>peripheral vascular disease</u>)

* Insufficient venous drainage (e.g., <u>chronic venous disease</u>)

* <u>Lymphedema</u>

* <u>Peripheral neuropathy</u>

* Sustained pressure (<u>decubitus ulcers</u>)

* Excessive tension on the wound edges [[9]](/library/nAd74s0)

* Repeated local trauma

* History of <u>radiation therapy</u> to the site

* Presence of a foreign body (e.g., orthopedic hardware) [[1]](/library/mAdV4s0)

* Other factors

* Older age

* Use of <u>tobacco products</u> [[10]](/library/WZVP0G0)

* <u>Social determinants of health</u> including <u>barriers to accessing health care</u> [[11]](/library/KAdUks0)
